pass_a_gloss:
A proclamation from life to life, to journey from light to light, from day to day, not to grow old but to be renewed, to receive renewal in the time of completion. He came in the Spirit to the temple. The spring led the thirsty one to the spring. When the parents brought the child Jesus to do for him what was customary, he received him in his arms. He carried in his hands the one who holds the inhabited and uninhabited world, who measured the water and the heaven with his hand and all the earth with a span. And how did Simeon offer a sacrifice not fitting for him? For he was not a priest. It was not said, nor was he a Levite or a temple servant, since the priestly service was allotted to the tribe of Levi alone. He was not a priest, but righteous. Righteousness has priesthood under its feet. He was not a Levite, but devout. The devout one has an anointing from himself. And carrying the child, he said: Now you release your servant, Master, according to your word in peace. Now you release: for the time of release has come, the redemption of captives has responded, the forgiveness of debts. A king was born, freeing those in prison, releasing those in bonds, calling back to life those in death, lightening the burden of the earth. Now you release your servant, Master. How do you know? I see the Master clothed in the form of a servant.

The master would not have taken on the form of a slave if he had not considered the slave to put on the form of the master. He would not have changed his position, nor would he have humbled himself if he had not wanted to elevate the humble. How can you release him according to your word in peace? If you brought creation into being by your word, you will certainly free the ruler of creation by your word. In what peace? The peace of the cross, for it beheaded the tyrant and gave peace to those who fight with Christ. I have seen the salvation you prepared, which many desired to see but did not see, God in the flesh, a sun shining in a cloud. I have seen your salvation, that is, your incarnation, through which you managed the salvation of humans. For no human has seen the naked divinity, since no one can see God as he is in essence. I have seen the salvation you prepared, which you have made according to the face of all peoples, a light for the revelation of nations and the glory of your people Israel. The good things are common and undivided for both Jews and Gentiles. Let not the Jew be envious, nor the Pharisee be distressed, nor the scribe be tempted, nor Herod be concerned about his kingdom, nor Annas and Caiaphas be afraid about their priesthood. He who came gives to all and receives from no one, generously and without measure bestowing gifts.

Mary wondered how a woman's womb contained God, how the servant gave birth to the one freeing creation. And she says this one lies for the fall and resurrection of many in Israel and for a sign being spoken against, for the fall of those persisting in unbelief
pass_b_english: The journey of life is a proclamation from one stage to another, where we transition from light to light, and from day to day, not to grow old but to be renewed in the time of completion. He came to the temple in the Spirit, as recorded in Luke 2:27. The spring led the thirsty one to the spring.
When the parents brought the child Jesus to the temple to perform the customary rituals, he was received in the arms of Simeon.

Simeon carried in his hands the one who holds the entire world, measuring the waters and the heavens with his hand, and all the earth with a span, as described in Isaiah 40:12. It is puzzling how Simeon, who was not a priest, could offer a sacrifice.
The priestly service was allotted to the tribe of Levi alone. Despite not being a priest, Simeon was considered righteous.
Righteousness is often seen as having a higher authority than the priesthood, with righteousness having priesthood under its feet. Simeon was not a Levite, but he was devout.
The devout one has an anointing from himself.

Carrying the child Jesus, Simeon said, 'Now you release your servant, Master, according to your word in peace,' as seen in Luke 2:29-32. The time of release had come, and with it, the redemption of captives and the forgiveness of debts.

A king was born, freeing those in prison, releasing those in bonds, and calling back to life those in death, thereby lightening the burden of the earth. Simeon's statement, 'Now you release your servant, Master,' marks the beginning of a new era. One might wonder how Simeon knew that the time of release had come. Simeon saw the Master clothed in the form of a servant.
The Master would not have taken on the form of a slave if he had not intended to elevate the humble.

How could he release his servant according to God's word in peace? If God brought creation into being by his word, he could certainly free the ruler of creation by his word. The peace of the cross, which beheaded the tyrant and gave peace to those who fight with Christ, is the peace that Simeon spoke of.
Simeon had seen the salvation that God had prepared, which many had desired to see but did not see - God in the flesh, a sun shining in a cloud.

This salvation was God's incarnation, through which he managed the salvation of humans. No human has seen the naked divinity, since no one can see God as he is in essence. Simeon had seen God's salvation, which was made according to the face of all peoples, a light for the revelation of nations and the glory of his people Israel.

The good things that God offers are common and undivided for both Jews and Gentiles. There should be no envy, distress, temptation, or concern among the Jews, Pharisees, scribes, Herod, Annas, and Caiaphas, for God's gifts are generously bestowed.

He who came gives to all and receives from no one, generously and without measure bestowing gifts. Mary wondered how a woman's womb could contain God, how the servant could give birth to the one who frees creation. And she says that this child lies for the fall and resurrection of many in Israel, and for a sign being spoken against, as mentioned in Luke 2:34, for the fall of those persisting in unbelief.

αὐτὸν «ἀπολύεις κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ;»· εἰ γὰρ ῥήματι τὴν κτίσιν παρήγαγες,

σου τὴν σάρκωσιν, δι' ἧς τὴν σωτηρίαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ᾠκονόμησας· οὐ γὰρ εἶδον
